newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli Jan-Sept chemical exports drop 3.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Israeli Jan-Sept chemical exports drop 3.9 pct.

text.p: Israeli chemical exports dropped 3.9 percent to $1.57 billion in the first nine months of 1996 compared with the same period a year ago, the Israel Manufacturers' Association said.
The chemical industry showed a negative trade balance for January to September this year, totalling about $82.5 million, association official Amir Makov said in a statement.
The figures did not include petroleum exports.
Makov said the drop in exports was a result of declining chemical prices worldwide and erosion of Israeli chemical manufacturers' profits due to largely frozen exchange rates for the shekel.
Some 42 percent of Israel's chemical exports are sent to European Community members, and another 21 percent goes to the United States.
